nodes.procedure: Self-supported electrodes of Ni, NiFe alloy, Ni(OH)₂, and NiFe-LDH were fabricated through one-step electrodeposition onto carbon cloths (see Figure S1 for details). The NiFe alloy and NiFe-LDH are denoted based on the Ni/Fe material molar ratio of 1:1.
nodes.source_text: Self-supported electrodes of Ni, NiFe alloy, Ni(OH)₂, and NiFe-LDH were fabricated through one-step electrodeposition onto carbon cloths, as illustrated in Figure S1. The NiFe alloy and NiFe-LDH are denoted based on the Ni/Fe material molar ratio of 1:1.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni and NiFe alloys possess densely packed nanoparticle morphology, whereas Ni(OH)2 and NiFe-LDH exhibit classic nanosheet structures.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) images show that Ni and NiFe alloys possess densely packed nanoparticle morphology, whereas Ni(OH)2 and NiFe-LDH exhibit classic nanosheet structures (Figures S2 and S3).

properties.description: secondary electron image showing particle morphology

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni and NiFe alloys have diffraction peaks corresponding to the face-centered cubic phase of metal Ni; reduced peak intensity for NiFe alloy suggests Fe doping causes atomic arrangement defects. No significant diffraction peaks for Ni(OH)2 and NiFe-LDH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The X-ray diffraction (XRD) patterns reveal that both Ni and NiFe alloys have diffraction peaks corresponding to the face-centered cubic phase of metal Ni (Figure S4a). The reduced peak intensity for NiFe alloy suggests that the doping of Fe atoms into Ni lattice caused atomic arrangement defects.

nodes.characterization_summary: Quasi-in situ Raman after CV cycles shows NiOOH formation (E_g at 475 cm⁻¹, A_1g at 552 cm⁻¹) strengthening on NiFe alloy in Fe-free KOH; NiFe-LDH shows stable O-M-O (196 cm⁻¹), Niᴵᴵ-O (467, 546 cm⁻¹), and OH peaks (304, 677 cm⁻¹) with intensity decline due to Fe coverage.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The peak at 533 cm⁻¹ for the initial pure Ni is attributed to Ni-O in the surface oxide film (Figure 2a). With more CV cycles in Fe-free KOH, this peak disappears and two new peaks appear at 475 and 552 cm⁻¹ corresponding to E_g and A_1g vibrations of Niᴵᴵᴵ-O, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni 2p: NiFe alloy shows Ni⁰ (852.0 eV) → Ni²⁺ (856.1 eV) after 200 CV; NiFe-LDH maintains Ni²⁺. Fe 2p: NiFe alloy Fe/Ni+Fe decreases 31.23→20.48%; NiFe-LDH increases 48.90→51.75%. O 1s shows increased O_v and decreased O_L for NiFe alloy, opposite for NiFe-LDH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Fe/Ni+Fe ratios obtained from the XPS results are shown in Table S1. The initial NiFe alloy shows the peaks attributed to Fe⁰ and Fe³⁺ at 707.2 and 712.7 eV, respectively. After 200 CV cycles, the whole peak signal becomes weaker and the Fe/Ni+Fe ratio decreases from 31.23 to 20.48%.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM shows lattice spacing of 0.26 nm matching (101) plane of NiFe-LDH and 0.24 nm matching (002) plane of NiOOH. Reconstructed amorphous phase forms on NiFe alloy after CV cycles.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) images reveal that a reconstructed amorphous phase formed on NiFe alloy (in Fe-free KOH) and Ni (in Fe³⁺-containing KOH) after 200 CV cycles (Figures 4a,b and S17).

nodes.characterization_summary: Elemental mapping shows uniform Fe distribution on Ni and Ni(OH)2 surfaces after CV in Fe³⁺-containing KOH; NiFe-LDH exhibits highest Fe content correlating with catalytic activity.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The elemental mapping images reveal the existence and uniform distribution of Fe on the surface of Ni and Ni(OH)2 after 200 CV cycles in Fe³⁺-containing KOH (Figure 4e-h).

nodes.characterization_summary: After 200 CV cycles, 3.62 μM Fe and 0.38 μM Ni leach from NiFe-LDH (5.9 and 4.2 times higher than NiFe alloy).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The leached Fe and Ni concentrations after the OER were determined by inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS). After 200 CV cycles, 3.62 μM of Fe and 0.38 μM of Ni leach from NiFe-LDH.

nodes.characterization_summary: EIS shows NiFe-LDH has lower R1 (self-oxidation) and R2 (OER resistance) than NiFe alloy; OER resistance unchanged after 200 CV cycles for NiFe-LDH due to Fe reabsorption.
nodes.evidence_snippet: After 200 CV cycles, Ni, NiFe alloy, and Ni(OH)2 in the Fe-free KOH show the increased OER resistances... Notably, the OER resistance of NiFe-LDH is essentially unchanged after 200 CV cycles in Fe-free conditions.
